text:
Maya: Heads up — flying red-eye tomorrow. looking for pocket books (under 300 pages) or <20-min essay/short-story recs. also craving low-effort late-night comedy shows to binge on a plane. any hidden gems?
Jordan: If you like weird and tiny: "The Sense of an Ending" by Julian Barnes — short but sticks with you. also the Simon Amstell special on Netflix is cozy late-night energy.
Devin: @Maya try 'Stoner' if you don't mind melancholic — ~250 pages. For dumb-late-night: 'I Think You Should Leave' episodes are perfect 15–20 min bursts. :laughing:
Sam: Pocket recs: "The Ocean at the End of the Lane" — ~181 pages, quick and oddly nostalgic. For comedy, shoutout to "People Just Do Nothing" if you haven't seen it (low stakes, big laughs).
Alicia: If you want essays, try Joan Didion's "The White Album" (one-off pieces, can stop/start). For lightweight comedy docs, "The Last Laugh" is surprisingly watchable.
Jordan: also small-fiction option: Lydia Davis flash fiction — a handful of stories are 2–3 minutes each. perfect for naps/short stretches between sleep attempts.
Maya: Ooh thanks all. Any recs that skew cheerful vs. heavy? prefer to avoid intense stuff on a red-eye.
Devin: Cheerful book: "The Rosie Project" is upbeat and breezy. Comedy: "Nate Bargatze: The Greatest Average American" — standup special, very gentle.
Sam: If you want purely silly, "Schitt's Creek" early seasons are warm and comforting (ep ~20 min).
Alicia: For micro-reads with a smile: "The Little Prince" reread — short and oddly uplifting.
Gloria (bot): GIF search: "red-eye sleep" :airplane: → 3 results (added to thread).
Maya: LOL @Gloria thanks. Last q: any audiobooks that are short and chill? plane wifi shaky but downloaded is fine.
Jordan: Audiobook: 'Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine' is longer but narrated so nicely you can drift. For very short, try recordings of classic short stories (Sherwood Anderson etc.) on LibriVox.
Devin: I grabbed a few Lydia Davis readings on podcast apps last week — super short episodes.
Sam: If you want music recs for sleeping on planes — mellow jazz or lo-fi playlist, but you asked for shows/books so will stop. :headphones:
Maya: Perfect. saved these. thanks y'all — will report back from 35,000 ft if I survive the in-flight movie choices :airplane::coffee:
